summary: Completed target-level planning pass for the concrete four-family arithmetic realisation, fixed-exponent Scholze support convention, transported continuous actions, and residual localization of the completed tower. Finite Hecke image theory is imported from its current upstream owner; CC.8 constructs its compatible inverse limit, proves stable residual support at a pro-p level, and forms its semilocal local factors and closed residual summands. The pass records exact finite geometry/comparison requests and noncommutative supplier gaps, without claiming proof closure or implementation.

nodes.title: Arithmetic tower realisation comparisons
nodes.statement: For each of the modular, Siegel, unitary and Hilbert families, fix the actual canonical-model tower X_K over its reflex field E, an embedding of an algebraic closure of E into C, a neat cofinal level system K=K_p K^p, and a compatible finite locally constant O/varpi^s coefficient system L_s from one chosen integral lattice. Identify the CC.0 finite-level arithmetic quotient with X_K(C), with its archimedean-component convention explicitly matched. The supplied finite étale–analytic comparison gives compatible O/varpi^s-linear isomorphisms of ordinary and compactly supported cohomology, natural for coefficient reduction, level pullback, finite étale trace and tame Hecke correspondences. Applying the existing CC.1 colimit at fixed s and then its inverse limit in s gives named continuous linear comparison isomorphisms between the generic completed objects and these four actual arithmetic towers. These are comparisons of the existing carrier, not four new definitions of completed cohomology. The boundary triangle is transported only for the compactification and support maps supplied by CC.2/CC.7.
hypotheses: O is the ring of integers in a finite extension of Q_p; varpi is a uniformizer; k is finite.
Neatness ensures finite-level schemes and covering maps; nonneat levels require the supplied stack or group-cohomology interpretation.

The connected real stabilizer A_infty^0 K_infty^0 used in the survey and the full stabilizer of a Shimura domain can differ. A comparison is asserted only after a concrete equivariant quotient dictionary; when descent is needed retain derived finite-component descent, rather than averaging at primes dividing the component-group order.

Siegel and unitary comparisons use the finite-coefficient portion of EDC.6/complex-analytic-comparison. R14.3 and R18.4 supply the modular and Hilbert/curve inputs. Trace comparisons use the chosen complex orientation.

For the complex orientation identify the finite Tate twist by the chosen compatible roots of unity. Use the EDC.6 trace-orientation input for Z/p^n and the supplied coefficient-extension compatibility for the selected O/varpi^s local system; no arbitrary unlabelled Tate-twist identification is made.
proofSteps: Import X_K, its canonical model, reflex-field action, and the analytic adelic quotient from V8; retain determinant/component labels, rather than silently selecting one geometric component.

Apply the exact finite-coefficient comparison with compact supports from EDC.6. For modular and Hilbert/curve families use the specialized local-system dictionaries in R14.3 and R18.4. Check all comparison squares before taking limits. Use EDC.6/trace-orientation-comparison for the chosen Tate-twist/complex-orientation normalization and CC.7 for its coefficient-system transport.

Use CC.1 functoriality on the cofinal level diagram at each s and CC.2/CC.7 for the support diagram. Then take the coefficient inverse limit with its induced topology; its inverse is the limit of the finite comparison inverses.
Export modularCompletedComparison, siegelCompletedComparison, unitaryCompletedComparison and hilbertCompletedComparison; R31.1 imports the first and fourth instead of constructing them again.

sources.match: The arithmetic quotient uses connected real stabilizers and retains a finite component-group action; this fixes the quotient dictionary required by the adapter.
The finite compact-support group is identified with étale cohomology of extension by zero on a compactification before the perfectoid argument. Only this finite comparison recipe is used here.

Ordinary finite-coefficient comparison and its constructible extension motivate the finite input; compact supports and naturality are imported from the stronger named EDC supplier, not inferred from this ordinary statement.

acceptance: On a finite disjoint union of geometric points the comparison preserves every component idempotent, and H^0 is the product of one coefficient module per component.
At the level of a noncompact modular curve, H_c^0=0 whereas H^0 contains constants; the support comparison must not substitute ordinary cohomology.
For a component group C_2 at p=2, no averaging projection using 1/2 is exported. The quotient dictionary or actual derived descent must appear.
The Galois action transported to the Betti object depends on the specified comparison and complex embedding; no Galois action on the bare singular site is asserted.

nodes.title: Definite unitary degree-zero adapter
nodes.statement: In the definite unitary setting of LLHLM §5.3, with fixed tame level U^p and fixed away-p lattice W, let S(U,W_s) consist of functions on G(F^+)\G(A_f) with f(gu)=u^{-1}f(g), W_s=W/varpi^s. The actual finite double quotient and its coefficient local system identify this module with H^0 of the finite arithmetic tower. Thus lim_s colim_{U_p} S(U_p U^p,W_s) is canonically the CC.1 completed degree-zero object for that tower, with its tame Hecke and G_p actions and coefficient-limit topology. At a nonneat finite quotient, the value at a representative x lies in W_s^{Gamma_x}; arbitrary W_s-valued functions are valid only when stabilizers act trivially. The degree-zero identification makes no claim that higher stabilizer cohomology vanishes. Galois representations associated to Hecke eigenvalues are not a Galois action on these functions.
hypotheses: Use the paper’s definite outer form of GL_3 over the totally real F^+≠Q, split over its CM field, and its specified local identifications and tame coefficient lattice.

For the simple G_p action by right translation, W is fixed away p and its U_p action is trivial. A nontrivial p-adic coefficient action requires the corresponding equivariant coefficient transport, not this simplified formula.
proofSteps: Use the finite double-coset decomposition to evaluate functions at representatives. Covariance identifies the result with the product of stabilizer invariants.
Identify the same invariant fibres in finite-level H^0 using the imported quotient/local-system dictionary. Verify coefficient and level maps, including the covariant coefficient action.

Apply CC.1 to this finite comparison; on the fixed away-p lattice use right translation to identify the G_p action and the standard finite Hecke sums. Import CC.3 for Pontryagin/Schikhof duals, rather than creating new dual carriers.

sources.locator: §5.3, pp. 120–122, especially the definitions of S(U,W), S(U^p,W) and its completed lattice
sources.match: These definitions specify the definite unitary group, coefficient covariance, fixed tame level and the coefficient/level limit order. The invariant-fibre formula follows directly from their covariance condition.

acceptance: One double coset with trivial stabilizer gives W_s, with the prescribed tame coefficient action.

For stabilizer C_2 acting by sign on O at p=2, integral invariant values are zero, while modulo 2 all values are invariant. Invariants cannot be interchanged with coefficient reduction without a descent theorem.
An empty double quotient gives the zero module; a disjoint union gives a product, not an identification with one selected component.

nodes.title: Scholze fixed-exponent support convention
nodes.statement: For the Hodge-type datum (G,D), the fixed embedding into (Sp_{2g},D_{Sp_{2g}}), and K^p contained in the level-N subgroup with N≥3 prime to p, Scholze’s tilde H^i_{c,K^p}(Z/p^n) in published §4.2 is colim_{K_p} H_c^i(X_{K_pK^p},Z/p^n), at fixed positive n. The compact-support part of the arithmetic comparison identifies this with the CC.1 fixed-coefficient object for the same tower, constant lattice Z_p and exponent n. The integral completed lattice is a separate lim_n construction; its modulo-p^n recovery requires CC.6 and is not the definition of the fixed-exponent object. This node supplies the left input and the boundary/support convention to TC.2. Scholze Theorem 4.2.1 and Corollaries 4.2.2–4.2.3, including the almost O_C coefficient tensor and the boundary ideal sheaf on the perfectoid minimal compactification, are exclusively TC.2 outputs.
hypotheses: n≥1 is fixed. Coefficients are exactly Z/p^n; an O/varpi^s variant requires an explicit coefficient extension receipt.
No perfection, almostification or automorphic sheaf is needed to construct this CC.8 object; those operations belong to TC.2.
proofSteps: Read the published §4.2 definition with the §4.1 Hodge embedding/tame level conventions, matching finite level and support with the arithmetic adapter.
Apply cofinality and the compact-support finite comparison at fixed n. Expose the level-insertion maps so TC.2 can verify its pullback/trace diagrams.
Register a supplier link CC.8→TC.2 for this fixed-exponent input. Preserve this integrated node id with its narrowed statement, and remove the perfectoid comparison output from CC.8 ownership.

sources.locator: §4.2, definition on p. 1020; Theorem 4.2.1 statement and its two level diagrams on p. 1021
sources.match: The definition is a compact-support colimit at fixed exponent with the Hodge/Siegel and tame-level hypotheses. The theorem is cited only to identify the consumer and its coefficient/support requirements, not as a CC.8 theorem.

acceptance: For a proper tower ordinary and compact supports agree under CC.2; for a nonproper connected curve they do not agree in degree zero.
The coefficient-limit lattice and its fixed quotient are not declared equal without the CC.6 coefficient-recovery hypotheses.
Changing the integral lattice changes the corresponding integral comparison; rational isomorphism alone is insufficient.

nodes.title: Transported Galois and Hecke actions
nodes.statement: On each actual finite geometric étale cohomology group of the canonical model over E, use its continuous G_E action and the chosen O-linear tame Hecke correspondence action defined over E. Transport them by the finite arithmetic comparison, then through the fixed-s level colimit and the coefficient inverse limit defining the existing completed object. The resulting actions are unique actions with those finite comparison squares; G_E and tame Hecke commute, as do both with G_p when supplied by the tower. Give the torsion level colimit the discrete topology and the integral object the inverse-limit topology. Require an open stabilizer for every torsion-colimit vector and continuous reduction maps. Then G_E×M→M is jointly continuous, and each Hecke operator is continuous. Joint continuity of G_p uses the analogous supplied open stabilizers, not just continuity of individual operators. On a rational object use the chosen stable integral lattice and its induced p-adic topology.
hypotheses: The finite Galois and Hecke actions commute with level pullback, coefficient reduction and the selected support maps. Actual Hecke correspondences descend over E.
An infinite-dimensional discrete colimit need not have an open global action kernel: require open point stabilizers, which suffice for joint continuity.
Full G_p action may move levels by conjugation; the CC.5 cofinal reindexing construction is supplied. Do not assume G_p acts on every fixed K_p group.
proofSteps: Conjugate the finite actions across the comparison, and use naturality to descend to each colimit. Prove its smoothness vector by vector at a finite level and finite coefficient.
Invoke the existing TopModuleCat limit and Functor.mapEnd on the coefficient diagram. Equality and commutation are checked under every limit projection; uniqueness follows from those projections.
For joint continuity, test each inverse-limit basic open using its discrete coordinate and that coordinate’s open stabilizer. Use CC.5 for G_p level reindexing and stable-lattice rationalization.
For each residual projector in this packet the commutation equations restrict these actions to its closed summand.

sources.match: The arithmetic tower carries the full p-adic group and completed tame Hecke action; CC.8 adds the canonical-model Galois transport to the generic construction.
The completed Hecke action commutes with the full p-adic group on completed homology. This is the consumer requirement for the transported action.

acceptance: Projection to each coefficient coordinate recovers the specified action, with the same order of Hecke composition.
A product of finite discrete representations gives a continuous inverse-limit action even when their common kernel is not open.

uses.how: The fixed-exponent compact-support comparison must retain commuting actions.
The Banach lattice and its residual summand must carry the same Galois, Hecke and G_p conventions.

nodes.title: Compatible finite derived Hecke image diagram
nodes.statement: Fix the commutative abstract spherical O-Hecke algebra H away from a finite set S containing p and all bad tame places. On each CC.4 perfect complex C_{U,s} over the finite group ring B_{U,s}=(O/varpi^s)[K_0/U], use the specified central O-linear derived H action and its finite faithful image T_{U,s}. For V⊂U and t≥s, require the actual Hecke-equivariant derived base-change identification B_{U,s} tensor-derived over B_{V,t} C_{V,t} ≅ C_{U,s}. It induces a surjective O-algebra homomorphism T_{V,t}→T_{U,s}, taking the class of h to the class of the same h. With the CC.4 coherence receipts these maps form a cofiltered diagram of finite commutative rings. Mere intertwining of homology maps does not construct these image-ring maps. The finite image, finite local factors, ghost bounds and derived idempotent splitting are IHG.2 inputs; CC.8 plans their compatible tower diagram.
hypotheses: U ranges over open normal subgroups of K_0, with a cofinal countable subsystem chosen for prototypes; finite images are finite as sets, not just finitely generated modules.
B_{U,s} can be noncommutative. The finite image contracts must be O-linear in D(B_{U,s}); IHG’s existing commutative-base Suggested.lean is not silently an equivariant noncommutative contract.
Use one compatible H and one common bounded cohomological interval for the family when exporting uniform ghost results.
proofSteps: Request the finite equivariant image/idempotent/ghost contract from IHG.2, with the existing commutative-base statements as its specialization. Verify finite cardinality from a bounded finite projective group-ring representative.

Apply derived coefficient change to each Hecke endomorphism. Since the same abstract H acts at the target, the source action kernel is contained in the target kernel; form the quotient/image map and prove surjectivity on H classes.
Check identity/composition using the actual CC.4 base-change isomorphisms and their coherence. Expose the image ring functor without reintroducing the finite Hecke algebra theory.

sources.match: The finite rings are images in the derived category of finite group-ring modules, and their transitions come from coefficient-change identifications, including reduction through a normal subgroup at nonnormal levels.

acceptance: Every transition is surjective on actual image rings and preserves the class of each abstract Hecke operator.
An operator killed in the finer derived image is killed after actual derived coefficient change.

uses.how: The big algebra is the inverse limit of this specific finite-image diagram.
Compatible image maps carry finite local factors and their projectors.

nodes.title: Residual support at a pro-p level
nodes.statement: Choose an open pro-p U_0⊂K_0, restrict to V normal in K_0 contained in U_0, and put A_0=T_{U_0,1} (formed by the same coefficient-change construction, permitting U_0 nonnormal through a smaller normal subgroup). Under finite equivariant images, bounded perfect complexes, the Hecke-equivariant derived coinvariant identification k tensor-derived over (O/varpi^s)[U_0/V] C_{V,s} ≅ C_{U_0,1}, and conservative derived residue reduction for those perfect complexes, each surjection T_{V,s}→A_0 induces a bijection of maximal ideals. Equivalently its kernel is contained in the Jacobson radical of the finite ring and is nilpotent. The maximal ideals are indexed by the support of the actual derived image, not by arbitrary maximal ideals of H.
hypotheses: U_0/V is a finite p-group. This hypothesis is essential.
The conservative reduction is required after splitting each Hecke residual idempotent; its summand is a perfect complex over the finite local group ring.
Ghost nilpotence identifies the support of a faithful derived image with the union of its homology supports; no equality of derived and homology images is assumed.
proofSteps: Split a finite residual factor using the IHG equivariant idempotent contract. A nonzero factor acts on a nonzero perfect summand: if its identity vanished on all cohomology, bounded ghost nilpotence would force that idempotent to vanish.

Over the local finite p-group algebra, conservative derived residue reduction detects this nonzero perfect summand. One can use a minimal representative with differentials in its radical, as in Gee–Newton 2.1.6–2.1.9; after residue reduction its nonzero free term survives. The P7 noncommutative extension is an explicit supplier gap.

The coinvariant identification puts every finer residual label in the support at U_0,1. Surjectivity gives the converse. A finite commutative ring’s radical is nilpotent; conclude the stated kernel criterion.

sources.locator: Lemma 2.1.14, p. 11; Definitions 2.1.6–2.1.8 and Proposition 2.1.9, pp. 9–10
sources.match: The pro-p residual support argument is the first part of the semilocality proof. Minimal complexes over a possibly noncommutative local ring provide an alternative rigorous detection argument with a named prerequisite.

acceptance: For a trivial tower A_0=k×k, exactly two residual labels persist.
For the C_2 sign representation over F_3, derived coinvariants vanish because 2 is invertible; a nonzero perfect summand can disappear. The pro-p hypothesis cannot be removed.
Nilpotent ghosts can change an image algebra but cannot create a new residual maximal ideal.

nodes.title: Completed derived Hecke algebra
nodes.statement: For the compatible finite derived-image diagram F of this packet define T_hat as its inverse limit, the subring of the product consisting of compatible tuples, with the subspace topology of the product of finite discrete rings. This is the instance of Mathlib RingCat.sectionsSubring attached to F, not a new generic inverse-limit construction. It is a compact Hausdorff complete topological commutative O-algebra. The evaluation maps to finite images are continuous surjections. The compatible map H→T_hat has dense image; it need not be surjective. Cofinal normal-level systems and iterated coefficient/level limits give canonical topological ring isomorphisms. The supplied finite actions induce a continuous action on the compatible CC.4 chain/homology system and its completed limit; on completed cohomology use the CC.3 adjoint/dual convention or an explicitly supplied cohomological diagram.
hypotheses: The normal-level/coefficient index is nonempty and cofiltered; transitions are surjective finite ring maps. Use a countable cofinal subsystem only after proving cofinality.
The completed module action is asserted only on diagrams whose action and transition maps are compatible and jointly continuous at each discrete coefficient level.
proofSteps: Apply the existing sections subring to the ring functor. The compatibility equations define a closed subset of the product of finite Hausdorff spaces; compactness, Hausdorffness and completeness follow.

For a finite coordinate or finite compatible set of coordinates, choose one finer coordinate. Finite surjective transitions and compactness lift it to a compatible tuple; images of H surject onto that finer image ring, proving density.

Use the limit universal property to compare cofinal/iterated systems. Apply compatible finite actions coordinatewise to CC.4 completed homology; use CC.3 rather than equating chain, homology and dual actions.

sources.match: These give the inverse limit, its topology, the iterated coefficient/level presentation and its action on completed homology.

acceptance: No topology of pointwise convergence on End(completed homology) replaces the specified inverse-limit topology.
The underlying ring and projections agree with the native compatible-sections carrier.

uses.how: The finite residual support produces finitely many completed local factors.
The GL_2 completed Hecke algebra specializes this common construction instead of constructing another big algebra.

nodes.title: Semilocal product decomposition
nodes.statement: Let T_hat be the preceding inverse limit and fix the finite base image A_0 of residual-support-stability. Then evaluation q:T_hat→A_0 is surjective and ker(q) is contained in J(T_hat). Pullback gives a bijection MaxSpec(A_0)≅MaxSpec(T_hat), including algebraic maximal ideals, not only continuous ones. With this finite index set, T_hat≅∏_m T_hat_m as rings and as topological rings when each factor is endowed with the inverse-limit topology from its finite local factors. Each T_hat_m is a compact complete Hausdorff local ring with the same finite residue field as the corresponding A_0 factor, and equals the algebraic localization of T_hat at m. The topology asserted here is the finite-image inverse-limit topology. No noetherianity, finite O-module assertion, or identification with the algebraic J-adic topology is inferred merely from semilocality.
hypotheses: Every finite transition is surjective and its map to A_0 has radical kernel. Finite local-factor decompositions and their uniqueness are supplied by IHG.2.
For the zero image system, the maximal spectrum is empty and the empty product is the one-element ring.
proofSteps: An element is a unit in the limit exactly when all its finite coordinates are units: their unique inverses form a compatible tuple. For x in ker(q) and any y, every coordinate of 1−yx is a unit because each finite kernel is radical. Thus ker(q)⊂J(T_hat), which treats all algebraic maximal ideals.

Use surjectivity of q to identify the finite maximal spectrum. Match each finite local factor to its A_0 label. Ring maps preserve its unique central idempotent, so finite decompositions are compatible.

Take the finite product of inverse-limit factors. The coordinatewise splitting and recombination are inverse continuous ring maps. Each factor has radical kernel over its finite local base, hence is local; elements outside its maximal ideal are units. The projection’s algebraic universal property identifies it with localization.

This proves the needed semilocal/topological decomposition directly, without relying on the stronger J-adic conclusion in the source proof. Export that stronger conclusion only with an additional closed-powers/completeness proof.

sources.match: The source states semilocality, residue finiteness and the local product decomposition. This node proves the inverse-limit-topology portion directly and leaves the source’s stronger algebraic radical-adic conclusion outside its claimed output.

acceptance: A constant k×k diagram has two algebraic maximal ideals and two factors.
For T={(a,b)∈O×O : a≡b mod varpi}, the ring is local: it has two rational eigensystems but only one residual factor.
An inverse system of local finite rings with arbitrarily large embedding dimensions may yield a nonnoetherian local limit; this theorem exports no noetherian instance.

nodes.title: Compatible residual Hecke projectors
nodes.statement: Given a residual maximal ideal m_0 of A_0, let e_{m_0,U,s} be the unique central idempotent of T_{U,s} equal to 1 in the local factor labelled m_0 and 0 in its other local factors. Their compatible tuple is e_{m_0}∈T_hat. This is the unique idempotent with those finite evaluations. The finite family is pairwise orthogonal and sums to 1, and e_{m_0}T_hat is the m_0-labelled completed local factor. It is independent of the chosen finite residual base, pro-p level and cofinal normal subsystem after the labelled transition identifications. A maximal ideal of the abstract H is eligible only if it lies in the finite-image residual support and is pulled back from m_0.
hypotheses: The finite local decomposition and residual-label bijections are fixed by the preceding theorem.
Do not lift separate characteristic-zero eigencharacters that are congruent modulo varpi to distinct integral projectors.
proofSteps: Use the unique finite local-factor idempotents from IHG.2. The residual-label bijections show that transition maps preserve them.
Form their element of the existing sections ring, and check idempotence, orthogonality and the finite sum at every coordinate.
Use cofinality and the unique finite evaluations to prove choice independence. Identify the image ideal with the corresponding product factor.

sources.match: The inverse-limit image algebra and its product into local factors provide canonical residual idempotents. This construction makes the projector compatibility and choice independence explicit.

acceptance: A residual ideal outside the image support is rejected as input; it does not define an arbitrary new summand.

uses.how: Its action defines the exact closed summand on the existing completed object.
Both consumers select the same residual factor, with congruent characteristic-zero eigensystems kept together.

api.name: TauCeti.CompletedArithmetic.residualProjector

nodes.title: Residual localisation of the completed tower
nodes.statement: For a compatible continuous T_hat action on the existing completed cohomology/homology object M, define its localisation at the supported residual ideal m_0 to be the image of the continuous idempotent operator P_{m_0}=e_{m_0} acting on M, with its subspace topology. Use the native linear-map range; do not define another completed carrier. For Hausdorff M it is closed, and M is the topological direct product of these finitely many images. Algebraically this image agrees with localization at the corresponding maximal ideal of T_hat, by the semilocal product theorem. The inclusion and projection split continuously. On CC.4 complexes take the corresponding compatible derived idempotent summands supplied by IHG.2. On a cohomological dual object use the adjoint-transposed Hecke convention from CC.3; the residual label is transported along that adjoint anti-isomorphism, not assumed unchanged.
hypotheses: T_hat acts continuously and its finite projectors agree with the finite diagram actions on M. The native idempotent image construction is reused from Mathlib.
The cohomology/homology duality identification and Hecke adjoints must be supplied by CC.3 for the stated supports and coefficient lattice.
proofSteps: Apply the ring action to e_{m_0}; its idempotence gives a continuous idempotent operator. Take its native linear range with induced topology.

Use Mathlib’s idempotent range=kernel(1−P) and closed-range theorem. Restrict the operator to obtain a split continuous projection and inclusion; finite orthogonal projectors yield the topological product.

Use the algebraic localization universal property of the ring factor to compare module localization. Use the imported derived splitting for complexes and the CC.3 adjoint action for cohomology versus homology.
Restrict commuting Galois, G_p and tame Hecke actions to the summand. No localization by an arbitrary abstract H ideal outside the supported finite spectrum is exported.

nodes.title: Localisation through limits, supports and duality
nodes.statement: For a compatible residual label on the actual completed tower, localisation commutes with the fixed-coefficient filtered level colimit and with the coefficient inverse limit: e(lim_s colim_U M_{U,s}) is continuously isomorphic to lim_s colim_U e_{U,s}M_{U,s}, with the inherited topologies. It also commutes with cofinal reindexing and with all supplied equivariant morphisms, including Galois and tame Hecke actions. For a supplied equivariant support triangle, applying compatible derived projectors gives its residual summand triangle and the induced localized long exact sequence. For the exact CC.3 Pontryagin/Schikhof duality pair, the transpose projector selects the dual of the original residual summand, with the adjoint Hecke label. This is not a claim that an arbitrary algebraic dual commutes with arbitrary inverse limits.
hypotheses: All finite projectors, transition maps and support-triangle maps are compatible. There are finitely many residual labels.
Topology and duality are the regimes of CC.1–CC.3; use CC.6 for integral-to-fixed-coefficient recovery, retaining lim^1 terms when its hypotheses fail.
proofSteps: At each fixed s, represent a vector at some finite level; applying its projector produces a representative in the selected finite summand. Orthogonal complements show the resulting filtered-colimit image comparison is bijective.

At the coefficient limit, send a compatible vector to its coordinate projections and use coordinatewise inclusion as inverse on the selected range. Continuity is tested under every coordinate map; no exactness of arbitrary inverse limits is used.

For support triangles use the already equivariant CC.2/CC.7 triangle and its functorial IHG splitting. For duality transpose the split inclusion/projection; use the exact CC.3 continuous dual comparison and coefficient/support regime.

sources.match: Residual localization is compatible with the completed homology object and the augmentation identification. The general CC.8 compatibility is a split-idempotent argument on the supplied diagrams, not a new augmentation or duality theorem.
The unitary example keeps a completed lattice and its dual, illustrating why dual localization must preserve the fixed lattice and its coefficient convention.

acceptance: For a constant O^2 tower with first-coordinate projector, both orders of limits/localization give the first coordinate with its original topology.
Localizing the boundary triangle preserves all three terms; it cannot replace compact support by the image in ordinary cohomology.
For a pairing between a module and its continuous dual, transpose the first-coordinate projector; a Hecke adjoint that permutes residual labels permutes the dual factor accordingly.

nodes.title: Derived and homology images have the same residual labels
nodes.statement: Suppose the finite derived image diagram T_i maps surjectively and compatibly to the corresponding image T_i^H on the direct sum of finite homology groups, and all complexes have cohomology in one common interval [a,b], a≤b. The induced map of finite-ring inverse limits T_hat→T_hat^H is surjective and its kernel has (b−a+1)-st power zero. Consequently it induces a bijection of residual maximal ideals and transports the unique residual projectors. It need not be an isomorphism. An action on one completed homology degree, or on End of its completed limit, is a further quotient and is not identified with either all-degree inverse-limit image algebra without a separate theorem.
hypotheses: Finite-ring diagrams share the same cofiltered index and compatible image-quotient maps. A uniform cohomological interval supplies the uniform exponent.
The IHG equivariant ghost bound is required in the actual derived category of the group-ring complexes.
proofSteps: Use the IHG bounded ghost theorem at every finite coordinate. Products of b−a+1 compatible ghost elements vanish at every coordinate and hence in the sections ring.

Surjectivity of the inverse-limit quotient uses compactness: for a fixed compatible homology-image tuple the finite fibres and finite transition constraints have the finite-intersection property, since a common finer coordinate can be lifted. Arbitrary inverse limits of surjections between infinite modules would not justify this step.
Apply the nilpotent-quotient maximal-spectrum and unique idempotent-lift comparison from the finite/complete Hecke input; label and projector compatibility follows. Do not identify the two rings.

sources.match: The finite derived image has nilpotent kernel on all homology; its residual support is therefore detected on homology. This node states the uniform-amplitude inverse-limit extension with its additional compactness hypotheses.

acceptance: A constant quotient k[epsilon]/epsilon^2→k has identical residual labels and projector 1 but is not an isomorphism.
Without a uniform exponent, coordinatewise nilpotent kernels need not yield a nilpotent limit kernel; the uniform-amplitude hypothesis stays in the statement.
